Subject: Nimbus RFP — follow-up on international exports and DPA annex

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the RFP submission. Our legal team reviewed the draft DPA Annex and had a few clarifying questions related to cross-border exports and the DPF-related controls, specifically for processing EU patient data in the US and APAC failover regions. Can you confirm the following: 

- Which specific transfer mechanisms Redwood relies on when serving EU data from hosted infrastructure (SCCs, DPF, or reliance on adequacy decisions)?
- Do you offer an implementation of the DPA Annex with clause-level editable sections for customer-approved redlines?
- For dedicated/private deployments, what operational controls are implemented to prevent inadvertent routing to non-authorized regions (examples: IP whitelisting, VPC egress controls, routing policies)?

A quick evidence pack (control mappings + a redline-friendly DPA Annex template) would be ideal. Our procurement timeline is tight — can you get us initial answers and any attachments by early next week?

Best,
Elena
Elena Costa
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Nimbus Health

Subject: Re: Nimbus RFP — follow-up on international exports and DPA annex

Elena — thanks for the clear list of asks. Looping in Rishi (Security/compliance) and Monica (Solutions/implementations) to provide the technical/evidence pack. 

High level answers up front:
1) Transfer mechanisms: For hosted accounts we rely on a combination of (a) standard contractual clauses where required, (b) customer choice to pin regional deployments (EU-only deployments available), and (c) for select customers we offer DPF supplementary safeguards mapped in the annex. We do not rely solely on an adequacy decision unless the customer specifically requests region pinning in an adequacy jurisdiction.

2) DPA Annex edits: We provide a redline-friendly DPA Annex template in Word; customers may propose clause-level edits. For enterprise legal review we have a standard playbook for negotiating changes that affect security or operational controls.

3) Dedicated/Private routing controls: For Redwood Dedicated and Private we enforce VPC egress controls, explicit region routing policies at the control plane, and optional IP allowlists. We also support an operational guardrail that preserves KV cache locality to avoid cross-region hot-reads. 

We'll send the evidence pack and annotated annex by Monday EOD.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Summary (short):
- Transfer mechanisms: Hosted API routes are anchored to region-specific clusters. For EU-processed data we operate under a combined approach: SCCs + documented supplementary safeguards when required by customer. We have a documented data export decision flow (see redwood_dpf_controls_v1.pdf) that explains how requests are routed, when we apply contractual safeguards, and where customer-configured region pinning occurs.

- Technical safeguards for hosted: TLS in transit, per-tenant encryption at rest, strict tenancy isolation. Optional customer-managed KMS for private deployments.

- Preventing cross-region routing: The control plane enforces region affinity; we have automated tests and a routing policy service that prevents route-promoting unless an emergency override is used (audited with two-person control). For Dedicated/Private: VPC egress rules + local KV caches with forced locality.

- Evidence: SOC2 summary and the control mapping provide control ids (CTRL-CRS-01..08) referenced in the annex template.

If you want we can set up a short technical walkthrough (30 min) to go through the routing flow diagrams on Tuesday.

Subject: RE: Redwood controls mapping and export mechanics (Nimbus request)

Elena — answers to your three follow-ups below and quick links.

1) Audit trail for routing overrides: Yes — every manual routing override is recorded in the control plane audit log with a timestamp, the operator id, the approval ticket id, and the justification. We capture two approver ids for production-level overrides and emit an immutable log entry shipped to our long-term audit store (retention default 7 years, configurable).

2) Non-negotiable clauses: From a security/ops perspective the following are non-negotiable: subprocessor flow-down requiring equivalent controls, encryption-in-transit and at-rest minimums (TLS 1.2+; AES-256 at rest), and incident notification windows (we can discuss specific hours but standard is 72-hour notification for incidents impacting confidentiality). Clause-level redlines that modify these controls will need escalation to our security governance team and may not be accepted. We'll mark these as "security critical" in the annex template.

3) SLA commitment on region enforcement: For Hosted we offer region-affinity guarantees documented in the contract (section on data residency). We will not serve EU-designated datasets from non-EU regions except for DR events that are declared in accordance with the DR runbook; each such event must be recorded and is auditable. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide stricter guarantees aligned to their capacity contracts.
